arkhangai.name: Arkhangai
arkhangai.lead: A green province on the northern slopes of the Khangai Mountains, rich in forested steppe, rivers and hot springs.
arkhangai.history: The Khöshöö Tsaidam monuments to Bilge Khagan and Kul Tigin of the Turkic Khaganate stand in Khashaat district. The present province was founded in 1931.
arkhangai.nature: In the west lie the crater of the extinct Khorgo volcano and Terkhiin Tsagaan Lake, formed when its lava flow dammed a river.

bayan-ulgii.name: Bayan-Ölgii
bayan-ulgii.lead: Mongolia's westernmost province, set among the high peaks of the Mongolian Altai.
bayan-ulgii.history: Founded in 1940. Most of its people are ethnic Kazakhs, who still keep the tradition of hunting with golden eagles.
bayan-ulgii.nature: Khüiten Peak in Altai Tavan Bogd is the highest point in Mongolia. Permanent snow, glaciers and alpine lakes are everywhere.
sights: Petroglyphic complexes of the Mongolian Altai

bayankhongor.name: Bayankhongor
bayankhongor.lead: Stretching from the Khangai Mountains down to the Gobi, it combines mountains, steppe and desert.
bayankhongor.history: Founded in 1941. Traces of Stone Age people were found in Tsagaan Agui (White Cave) in Bayanlig district.
bayankhongor.nature: The Khangai range rises in the north, the Valley of the Lakes crosses the middle, and the Gobi-Altai range and desert fill the south.

bulgan.name: Bulgan
bulgan.lead: A forest-steppe province along the Orkhon and Selenge river basins.
bulgan.history: Founded in 1938. Dashinchilen district holds the Khitan-era ruins of Khar Bukh Balgas and the 17th-century White House of Tsogt Taij.
bulgan.nature: Extinct volcanoes such as Uran Togoo, forests and fertile valleys.

govi-altai.name: Govi-Altai
govi-altai.lead: A vast province spanning the Mongolian Altai, the Gobi-Altai range and the great Gobi.
govi-altai.history: Founded in 1940. It is the second-largest province by area.
govi-altai.nature: The Great Gobi Strictly Protected Area is home to the rare Gobi bear (mazaalai) and the wild Bactrian camel.

govisumber.name: Govisümber
govisumber.lead: A small province along the railway, with the smallest population in the country.
govisumber.history: Once part of Dornogovi. Choir was a separate municipality before being organised as a province.
govisumber.nature: Lies in the transition zone between steppe and Gobi, with coal deposits.

darkhan-uul.name: Darkhan-Uul
darkhan-uul.lead: An industrial province around Darkhan, Mongolia's second-largest city.
darkhan-uul.history: Darkhan was founded in 1961 and developed as an industrial centre. It became a province in 1994.
darkhan-uul.nature: Located in the Kharaa river valley, well suited to farming.

dornogovi.name: Dornogovi
dornogovi.lead: A south-eastern Gobi province crossed by the Ulaanbaatar–Beijing railway.
dornogovi.history: Founded in 1931. The 19th-century lama and poet Danzanravjaa founded Khamar Monastery here.
dornogovi.nature: Gobi desert and steppe. Zamyn-Üüd is the main border crossing with China.

dornod.name: Dornod
dornod.lead: Mongolia's easternmost province: a vast sea of grassland steppe.
dornod.history: Founded in 1941. The 1939 Battle of Khalkhin Gol took place here.
dornod.nature: Untouched grasslands such as the Menen steppe host great herds of Mongolian gazelle. The Khökh Lake depression is the country's lowest point.

dundgovi.name: Dundgovi
dundgovi.lead: The 'Middle Gobi' province, south of Ulaanbaatar.
dundgovi.history: Founded in 1942. The ruins of Ongi Monastery lie on the banks of the Ongi river in Saikhan-Ovoo district.
dundgovi.nature: A transition zone between steppe and Gobi, known for granite rock formations and eroded cliffs.

zavkhan.name: Zavkhan
zavkhan.lead: Running from the western Khangai Mountains to the Great Lakes Depression.
zavkhan.history: Uliastai grew from a Manchu-era garrison town in the 18th century. The province was founded in 1931.
zavkhan.nature: Snow-capped Otgontenger is the highest peak of the Khangai range. Sand dunes, lakes and rivers sit side by side.

orkhon.name: Orkhon
orkhon.lead: The smallest province by area, a mining region centred on the city of Erdenet.
orkhon.history: The city grew up after the Erdenet copper and molybdenum plant opened in 1978. It became a province in 1994.
orkhon.nature: Surrounded by Bulgan province, in the forest-steppe zone.

selenge.name: Selenge
selenge.lead: Along the northern border; the country's main farming region.
selenge.history: Founded in 1934. The 18th-century Amarbayasgalant Monastery is one of the largest monasteries to survive intact.
selenge.nature: The confluence of the Orkhon and Selenge rivers, forest-steppe and fertile valleys.

sukhbaatar.name: Sükhbaatar
sukhbaatar.lead: A south-eastern province, home of the extinct volcanoes of Dariganga.
sukhbaatar.history: The province is named after D. Sükhbaatar. The Dariganga area has many ancient stone figures.
sukhbaatar.nature: Steppe, extinct volcanoes, sand dunes and small lakes.

tuv.name: Töv
tuv.lead: The central province that surrounds the capital, Ulaanbaatar.
tuv.history: Founded in 1931. The ruins of the 18th-century Manzushir Monastery lie on the slopes of Bogd Khan mountain.
tuv.nature: Western spurs of the Khentii range and the Tuul river basin. Przewalski's horses (takhi) were reintroduced in Khustai National Park.

uvs.name: Uvs
uvs.lead: A north-western province in the Great Lakes Depression.
uvs.history: Founded in 1931. Dörvöd, Bayad and Khoton peoples make up most of its population.
uvs.nature: Uvs Lake is Mongolia's largest lake by area, and its basin is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

khovd.name: Khovd
khovd.lead: Spanning the Mongolian Altai and the Great Lakes Depression, the homeland of many ethnic groups.
khovd.history: Khovd town grew up in the Manchu era in the 18th century. Khoit Tsenkher cave preserves Stone Age rock paintings.
khovd.nature: Snow-capped mountains, the Khar-Us, Khar and Dörgön lakes, and the Gobi side by side.

khentii.name: Khentii
khentii.lead: The Khentii Mountains and the Onon and Kherlen river basins — the birthplace of Chinggis Khaan.
khentii.history: Delüün Boldog in Dadal district is held to be Temüjin's birthplace. The provincial centre, Öndörkhaan, was renamed Chinggis City in 2013.
khentii.nature: Taiga in the north and steppe in the south. The sacred landscape around Burkhan Khaldun is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

khuvsgul.name: Khövsgöl
khuvsgul.lead: A northern province of taiga, mountains and the great Lake Khövsgöl.
khuvsgul.history: Founded in 1931. Bronze Age deer stones stand at Uushigiin Övör near Mörön.
khuvsgul.nature: Lake Khövsgöl is Mongolia's deepest lake and holds the most fresh water. Reindeer-herding Tsaatan families live in the taiga.

uvurkhangai.name: Övörkhangai
uvurkhangai.lead: On the southern slopes of the Khangai Mountains — the cradle of Mongolian history.
uvurkhangai.history: Karakorum, capital of the Mongol Empire, stood here. Erdene Zuu Monastery was built on its ruins in 1586.
uvurkhangai.nature: The Orkhon Valley is a UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape. Mountains in the north give way to Gobi in the south.

umnugovi.name: Ömnögovi
umnugovi.lead: The largest province by area: the heart of the Gobi.
umnugovi.history: Founded in 1931. Dinosaur eggs found at Bayanzag in the 1920s made it famous worldwide.
umnugovi.nature: The Gurvan Saikhan range, sand dunes and saxaul Gobi. The Oyu Tolgoi and Tavan Tolgoi deposits are here.
